title: Human approval authority
context: Agents can propose and implement work but do not own product or release decisions.
problem: Make authority and approval boundaries explicit and auditable.
options_considered: Human retains final authority over major and consequential decisions.
Allow agents to silently change approved decisions or perform consequential work.
decision: The human project owner retains final authority over requirements, major architecture, security-sensitive changes, data migration, destructive operations, releases, and changes to accepted decisions.
rationale: Consequential product and operational decisions require explicit human control.
consequences: Agents may propose decisions but must label them Proposed until explicitly approved.
Ordinary reversible implementation within an approved task does not require repeated approval.
